options.counterfactual: Every norm-bounded increasing sequence of positive elements in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, even when its quasitrace is not known to be additive.
options.approach: Investigate the precise monotone sequential completeness theorem for finite AW*-factors, distinguishing it from completeness of their projection lattices. If its hypotheses match the problem, apply it directly to show that the required absence of a least upper bound is impossible.

options.counterfactual: Every norm-bounded increasing sequence of positive elements in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, even when its quasitrace is not known to be additive.
options.approach: Try to construct the supremum through the quasitrace metric: first establish that a bounded increasing sequence is Cauchy, then use metric completeness of the factor and verify that order passes to the limit.

options.counterfactual: Every norm-bounded increasing sequence of positive elements in a finite AW*-factor has a least upper bound, even when its quasitrace is not known to be additive.
options.approach: Investigate whether a bounded increasing sequence admits a projection dilation in an AW*-algebra containing the original factor as a corner. A sufficiently normal dilation would allow a projection supremum to produce the desired positive-element supremum by compression.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor can satisfy q(x)=q(y) for distinct positive elements x≤y.
options.approach: Study the spectral distributions of such comparable elements and identify how equality of their quasitraces can coexist with a positive difference. This could reveal the mechanism needed for persistent positive increments.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor can satisfy q(x)=q(y) for distinct positive elements x≤y.
options.approach: Investigate whether one comparable equal-value pair can be iterated, using corners or matrix amplification, to construct a bounded increasing sequence whose increments have uniformly positive quasitrace.

options.counterfactual: A faithful normalized 2-quasitrace on a finite AW*-factor can satisfy q(x)=q(y) for distinct positive elements x≤y.
options.approach: Analyze the equality conditions at η=1/2. Determine whether the resulting requirement that every nonempty finite sum of increments has quasitrace 1/2 can be realized consistently within a finite AW*-factor.

options.counterfactual: The set G is nonempty, but its supremum is strictly smaller than 1/2 because three or more increments impose a stronger restriction than the elementary two-increment bound.
options.approach: Analyze triples of positive increments with sum at most 1, looking for inequalities derived from the 2-quasitrace extension rather than from unproved additivity. Such an inequality could yield a bound below 1/2.

options.approach: Use spectral cutoffs to turn the increments into projections of uniformly positive dimension with bounded positive partial sums. Investigate whether finite-factor projection geometry supplies a sharper quantitative packing bound.

options.approach: Examine whether positive block matrices in M2(M) impose constraints on several increments simultaneously. The extension defining a 2-quasitrace may yield restrictions unavailable from monotonicity in M alone.
